reason: The cited lines show the tool takes a parsed `url` parameter and sends a `browser_navigate` socket message with that URL, so it can cause navigation/request to an agent-supplied URL, which is a SINK. In the snapshot-enabled registration (`navigate(true)`), after navigation it calls `captureAriaSnapshot`, which retrieves and returns the page URL, title, and browser snapshot; this can return page content from reachable private/local/intranet or credentialed pages, supporting SECRET, and because arbitrary navigated page content can be attacker-controlled, it also supports UNTRUSTED. The lines do not show arbitrary code execution on the host; browser navigation/page code is not HOSTEXEC.
